text:
dave: Hey support — after I upgraded the Python SDK via Poetry our production service started getting 401s from the Redwood API. Local dev works fine. Thought it was an auth/regression in SDK. Logs from the failing service below:
```
2024-06-25T03:12:11Z ERROR app.request: API call failed status=401 url=https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate body={...} headers={Authorization: 'Bearer ****' }
response: {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"invalid api key"}
```
I didn't change keys, same env var used in staging where it works. Any ideas?

lina: thanks — can you paste the output of `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__, redwood.__file__)"` from the running environment, and `pip show redwood-sdk` / `poetry show`? Might be a different package installed in prod. Also include how you deploy (systemd, docker, etc).

dave: quick answers: systemd service on Debian 12, python 3.11 from distro. Deploy user is `deploy`. I ran these on the host as the deploy user: 
```
$ python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__, redwood.__file__)"
'0.9.2' '/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/redwood_sdk/__init__.py'

$ pip show redwood-sdk
Name: redwood-sdk
Version: 1.4.0
Location: /home/deploy/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages
Requires: requests, aiohttp
```
So pip shows 1.4.0 in my user local site-packages, but import prints 0.9.2 from /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages. That looks like a system package shadowing the newer one.

kevin: yeah that jump stands out. The system distro package (maybe `python3-redwood-sdk` or a renamed package) is earlier and on sys.path before user site-packages when running systemd or a different PYTHONPATH. Systemd may run without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/home mount or with a different `PYTHONNOUSERSITE` setting.

lina: can you show the systemd service file (ExecStart) and the output of `python -c "import sys; print(sys.path)"` under the same user context the service runs as? Also confirm whether you installed the Poetry-managed wheel into the system env or are relying on `pip install --user` in CI.

dave: service file snippet: 
```
[Service]
User=deploy
Environment=REDWOOD_API_KEY=****
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/myapp/app.py
```
And when I run as deploy user in a normal shell, `sys.path` contains `/home/deploy/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages` before `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages`. But systemd runs a very minimal env. I just tried `sudo -u deploy /usr/bin/python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.path)"` and it prints `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages` ahead of the user site.

kevin: that's the smoking gun — systemd's invocation (non-login) can cause the user site to be ignored / not added early. If the old distro package is on sys.path earlier, import will resolve to v0.9.2. That older version probably uses a different auth header format or an old validation that results in 401.

lina: for repro you can run the exact ExecStart under the same minimal environment (systemd-run --user or sudo -u) to reproduce. For a fix: either remove the distro package (`apt remove python3-redwood-sdk`), vendor the correct SDK into a virtualenv (recommended), or modify service to use the virtualenv's python: `ExecStart=/opt/venvs/myapp/bin/python /opt/myapp/app.py`. Also `pip install --user` is unreliable for system services.

support-bot: :information_source: Suggested quick commands:
```
# show which package will be imported by default
python3 -c "import importlib.util, redwood, sys; print(redwood.__file__)"
# force reinstall into system site if you must (not recommended for reproducible deploys)
sudo pip3 install --upgrade --force-reinstall redwood-sdk
# better: create venv and point systemd at venv python
python3 -m venv /opt/venvs/myapp && /opt/venvs/myapp/bin/pip install -r /opt/myapp/requirements.txt
```

dave: thanks — I removed the distro package and created a venv. After switching ExecStart to `/opt/venvs/myapp/bin/python /opt/myapp/app.py` the service started and the API calls now succeed (200). For reference the `import redwood` now prints `1.4.0 /opt/venvs/myapp/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_sdk/__init__.py`.

lina: great! closing notes: 1) avoid `--user` installs for services; 2) always pin the SDK version in your lockfile and deploy the lockfile-managed artifacts into a venv; 3) `python -c 'import redwood; print(redwood.__file__, redwood.__version__)'` is a fast way to validate which package is being used.

kevin: adding that if you see auth differences after an SDK upgrade also check the SDK release notes — sometimes default header behavior changes and older tokens might be rejected. But in this case shadowing was the root cause.

dave: confirmed — thanks a lot, saved me hours. :thumbsup:
